children: Space Exploration Technologies Corp.
earned an upgrade to Buy following a pivotal Q3 earnings reversal and successful Starship Flight 14 test results. Hawaiian Electric Industries
also received a significant upgrade from Strong Sell to Buy as risks have declined and projected returns have improved with the passage of time. On the downside, Tesla
faces a downgrade to Hold despite solid Q3 deliveries, with an analyst citing concerns over margin quality and elevated valuations. Amazon
similarly moved to Hold as heavy capital spending weighs on free cash flow generation.
Upgrades
Space Exploration Technologies
: Upgrade Hold to Buy by

The analyst points to SpaceX's FQ3 2026 positive EPS reversal, successful Flight 14 test demonstrating orbital insertion and Starlink satellite deployment, and regulatory filings for up to 456 annual Starship launches as key catalysts shifting the risk-reward profile.

"A range of new catalysts have promoted this revisit to SpaceX since my last coverage. The most consequential ones on my list are the successful Flight 14 test results, the EPS reversal reported in FQ3 earnings, and also the scaling up of its Starship program. These positives outweigh the downside risks and are sufficiently material in our model to cause a rating upgrade to Buy."
Hawaiian Electric Industries
: Upgrade Strong Sell to Buy by

The analyst believes risks associated with Hawaiian Electric have reduced over time while the shorter investment duration through post-wildfire normalization significantly improves projected annualized returns to 20.62%.

"My cautious self says Hold and wait for the risk to decline further and the required duration of investment to continue shrinking with the continuing passage of time, thus further boosting projected returns. At the same time, hesitation could see the opportunity slip away if the current share price turns out to be a bottom and the price moves upward again, and on that basis the stock is likely a Buy."
Downgrades
Tesla
: Downgrade Buy to Hold by

The analyst notes that Q3 margin improvement was substantially driven by tariff refunds rather than organic operational gains, while the $1.55 trillion market cap at $391 already prices in significant future success across FSD, Robotaxi, Optimus, and energy businesses.

"The margin improvement was substantially driven by tariff refunds while nine-month FCF continued to lag under $2 billion despite over $13 billion of capex. ... Since my last coverage, TSLA has gone nowhere, and at a $1.55 trillion market cap at $391, I think investors are already priced in for a lot of future success at Tesla, and that’s why I am downgrading the stock to Hold."
Amazon.com
: Downgrade Strong Buy to Hold by Ryan Canady.

The analyst is concerned that despite robust Q2 2026 growth in net sales and operating income, heavy capital expenditures—projected at approximately $220 billion for 2026—are consuming cash flow and preventing gains from reaching shareholders.

"I believe that it is wise to downgrade Amazon at this time based on its heavy spending. However, I am simply taking it down from a "strong buy" to a "hold" rating. I do believe that the quality of the business is still strong and that this is a name worth keeping an eye on."
